Jasmine,

Thanks for the proposal deck — overall this looks promising. Before we move to legal I have two key asks from procurement and finance:

Also attaching a short internal note (we can share legal redlines after we see redlineable term sheet).

- Yes: we can model a staged prepay with a 50/30/20 commit split and corresponding tiered unit pricing.
- Refunds / buyback: we typically offer a structured rebate for early termination (not a full cash refund) tied to how much of the committed credits were consumed vs reserved; we can map that to a waterfall.
- Co-terming: we support co-terming by amortizing the remaining committed value to the new co-term date or offering a one-time credit to align invoices.

Team / Tom,

Attached is a concise waterfall and a suggested Termination for Convenience sentence. Key points: 

- Proposed waterfall (summary):
  * Year 1 (50% commit): if terminated for convenience in Year 1, customer receives 85% of unconsumed prepaid value back as a cash rebate (subject to a 30-day reconciliation, excludes any consumed tokens).
  * Year 2 (30% commit): 60% rebate of unconsumed prepaid value.
  * Year 3 (20% optional): non-refundable but convertible to a one-time credit if customer elects to keep an enterprise support commitment.

- Termination for Convenience (draft sentence):
  "If Customer terminates this Agreement for convenience, Redwood will, within 30 days of termination, refund to Customer a percentage of the unconsumed prepaid amount equal to the applicable rebate percentage for the then-current contract year, less any outstanding fees or charges; refunds are payable to the invoiced party and are not transferable without Redwood's prior written consent."

- Co-terming handling: we are willing to provide a one-time cash credit payable to the invoiced party; credits are not automatically transferable to third-party reseller invoices. We can consider a direct payment to a named reseller under an agreed amendment and proof of entitlement.

Rationale: 85% in Year 1 balances AcmeSoft's cash protection ask while limiting Redwood's exposure. The escrow/amortization approach is still an option if AcmeSoft prefers staggered settlement.

Please review and tell us which approach (85/60/0 or escrow amortization) AcmeSoft prefers so we can finalize the term-sheet language and route to legal.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, Finance Operations, Redwood Inference

Tom — appreciate the feedback. High-level ask from leadership: we want to keep the deal economics achievable while minimizing forecasting risk. Proposal from our side:

- Accept the 85% Year 1 rebate (as Kimberly drafted) conditional on:
  1) a 90-day notice window for termination for convenience, and
  2) a minimum usage threshold in Year 1 (e.g., 25% of Year 1 commit) below which a stepped administrative fee of 5% applies to refunds to discourage strategic prepay/terminate behaviour.

- For co-terming: Redwood agrees to provide a cash refund to the invoiced party; if AcmeSoft requires funds be paid directly to a reseller, we will consider an amendment with named recipient and proof of entitlement (reasonable KYC).

Next steps: Jasmine / Aditya — if Tom agrees in principle, please ask AcmeSoft to circulate redlines to erin.shaw@acmesoft.com and we will have legal review the draft sentence. We can serialize the final waterfall into the term sheet and SOW.
